posts.title: ELIA Partners with Messe Frankfurt to Host the All Africa Leather Fair 2026
posts.summary: ELIA signed a partnership with Messe Frankfurt to host the All Africa Leather Fair alongside Africa Sourcing and Fashion Week (ASFW Addis), positioning Addis Ababa as a continental hub for leather fashion and sourcing.
posts.body:
ELIA signed a partnership with Messe Frankfurt to host the All Africa Leather Fair alongside Africa Sourcing and Fashion Week (ASFW Addis), positioning Addis Ababa as a continental hub for leather fashion and sourcing.

The All Africa Leather Fair 2026 takes place from 12 to 15 November 2026 at the Addis International Convention Center, Addis Ababa, held alongside ASFW Addis 2026. Its closing event is the ELIA Award and Gala Night on 15 November 2026 at the Sheraton Addis.

[About the fair](/programs#aalf)

posts.title: ELIA Raises Industry Priorities with Government
posts.summary: At a press briefing in Addis Ababa, ELIA President Zelalem Merawi called for stronger action on raw hide supply, access to finance and planned relocation of factories to serviced industrial parks.
posts.body:
At a press briefing in Addis Ababa, ELIA President Zelalem Merawi called for stronger action on raw hide supply, access to finance and planned relocation of factories to serviced industrial parks.

The Ministry of Industry outlined reforms to the raw hide marketing law and the development of Modjo Leather City.

[More on the industry](/industry)

posts.title: Why Trade Associations Matter in the Leather Industry
posts.summary: In many developing countries, competing leather businesses share interests that often go unrecognized. Working together through an association gives the industry a stronger voice with government and a better chance to grow.

posts.title: Ethiopian Highland Leather: From Raw Material to National Brand
posts.summary: How Ethiopia's highland sheepskin became a registered national brand, and what it means for producers and international buyers.
posts.body:
Ethiopian Highland Leather is the national brand of Ethiopian sheep leather, produced from sheep raised in the Ethiopian highlands. Developed in 2015 with support from the Ethiopia Industrial Promotion Project, the brand is owned and managed by ELIA and is registered in Ethiopia, the United States, Japan, the European Union and the United Kingdom.

## A material with a reputation

Research by the national leather institute confirms that Ethiopian highland sheepskin is light, thin and soft, yet strong and durable. It is valued worldwide for its fine grain, compact fibre structure and strength, and is a preferred material for premium gloves, footwear and leather goods. EHL leather is inspected by an internationally accredited national laboratory.

## Certified producers

- Davimpex Bahir Dar Tannery
- Ethio-Leather Industry PLC (ELICO)
- New Wing Shoe Manufacturer
- Pitards Ethiopia Tannery

## Why it matters

- **By-product:** a 100% by-product of the Ethiopian food culture.
- **Environment:** produced with extra care for the environment.
- **Jobs:** employment for many women and young people.
- **Fair value:** a premium price that helps reduce inequality in international trade.

[About Ethiopian Highland Leather](/ehl)
